moments.title: Ancient Egypt endured for so long that the pyramids were already ancient by the time Cleopatra ruled. The Great Pyramid had stood for roughly 2,500 years before she was born. In fact, Cleopatra lived closer in time to th
moments.selftext: Ancient Egypt endured for so long that the pyramids were already ancient by the time Cleopatra ruled. The Great Pyramid had stood for roughly 2,500 years before she was born. In fact, Cleopatra lived closer in time to the invention of the internet than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient Egypt endured for such an extraordinary length of time that its people eventually became historians and restorers of their own ancient past. The Great Pyramid of Giza was constructed around 2560 BCE, while Cleopatra VII lived from 69 to 30 BCE—nearly 2,500 years later. By the time she ruled Egypt, the pyramids were already relics of a civilization that stretched thousands of years into the past. Long before Cleopatra, Egyptian rulers and scholars were already studying, preserving, and restoring monuments that were ancient even to them. Prince Khaemweset, a son of Ramesses II who lived roughly 1,200 years before Cleopatra, became particularly well known for restoring temples and tombs that were already centuries old during his lifetime. Cleopatra lived during the final period of ancient Egypt’s long pharaonic era. She belonged to the Greek-speaking Ptolemaic dynasty, which came to power following Alexander the Great’s conquest of Egypt in 332 BCE. The immense span of this history can be difficult to grasp: Cleopatra lived closer to the invention of the internet than she did to the construction of the Great Pyramid.

moments.selftext: What is happening with the US job market? US job openings for June were revised down by -177,000 vacancies, their largest monthly downward revision since November 2025. This also marks the 3rd consecutive monthly downward revision. Furthermore, the number of hires for June was revised down by -16,000, while the number of quits was revised lower by -19,000. At the same time, the number of layoffs and discharges was revised up by +19,000. As a result, job openings have now been revised down in 38 of the last 43 months. US labor market data is becoming increasingly difficult to read with confidence.

moments.selftext: There is an employment recession in the US Information sector. The Information industry shed -23,000 jobs in August, bringing employment down to 2.75 million, its lowest since the 2020 pandemic. The Information sector includes software publishing, data processing and computing infrastructure, web search, telecom, broadcasting, publishing, and other information services. Excluding 2020, this is the lowest reading since April 2015. Since the November 2022 peak, Information employment has contracted -270,000, or -12%. By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and its aftermath, employment in this industry also fell -12%, or -350,000 jobs. AI is increasingly replacing skilled human labor across parts of the Information sector.

moments.title: “The highest form of peace is having no desire to be seen, validated or understood by anyone.” - Epictetus True inner peace comes from releasing the need to be accepted, validated, or completely understood by other peopl
moments.selftext: “The highest form of peace is having no desire to be seen, validated or understood by anyone.” - Epictetus True inner peace comes from releasing the need to be accepted, validated, or completely understood by other people. When you no longer depend on outside approval, you gain greater control over your own happiness and emotional well-being. Allowing the opinions of others to determine how you feel can make your sense of worth dependent on things that are ultimately beyond your control. Instead, focusing on your own values, character, and actions allows you to separate yourself from outside judgment and negativity. This sense of detachment can create lasting freedom because your self-worth comes from within rather than from the constantly changing opinions and perceptions of others.

moments.title: I think the next insane thing with Astra and 3D will be in manufacturing. Vibe-manufacturing with 3D printers en masse. In all sorts of materials. I’m obsessed with making things on my 3D printer and the biggest issue is
moments.selftext: I think the next insane thing with Astra and 3D will be in manufacturing. Vibe-manufacturing with 3D printers en masse. In all sorts of materials. I’m obsessed with making things on my 3D printer and the biggest issue is always the modeling time. My mom asked me a few weeks ago for a very rare part for her toilet that’s discontinued and I’ve not been able to locate the manufacturers drawing of it to properly model it. I have some photos of the broken part and measurements. Gave it to Astra, alongside with the rest of the info. Astra actually found some manual online with a small 2D drawing, combined with my photos and the measurements it was able to model the part in less than 2 minutes. It made a .stl file, sent it to my printer in Sweden, and 1.5h later the part was printed and ready for my mom to pick up. Absolutely nuts. Everything will be put on its head, hundreds of new multi million dollar businesses will be made. it’s still about creating the glue and value and ensuring repeatable outcomes. But holy cow, I’m just amazed by how incredibly powerful of a moment this is. this is the fusion of digital and physical. and we are just getting started. mindblown 🤯
